comparisons.peer_topic: Data Center Segment Product Portfolio and Strategy
comparisons.peer_summary: The Data Center segment includes server-class CPUs, GPUs, AI accelerators, DPUs, FPGAs, SmartNICs, and Adaptive SoC products. The company leverages these technologies to address computational, visual data processing, and AI workload acceleration needs by enabling optimization of performance and power for diverse workloads.
comparisons.comparison: Both MU and AMD identify data centers and AI as primary drivers for high-performance technology demand, but they address different layers of the infrastructure. MU focuses on storage solutions (SSDs) to handle data access and capacity for AI workloads, noting that 'Applications such as machine learning servers require fast access to data with low latency.' In contrast, AMD focuses on the compute layer, stating it 'leverage[s] our technology to address the computational, visual data processing and AI workload acceleration needs in the data center market' through CPUs and GPUs. While MU targets the storage bottleneck for AI data lakes, AMD targets the processing acceleration for those workloads.

sentences.text: Applications such as machine learning servers require fast access to data with low latency, predictable performance, and high storage capacities.
Our 6500 30TB SSDs features high performance, reliability, and endurance for AI data lake applications.
We leverage our technology to address the computational, visual data processing and AI workload acceleration needs in the data center market.
Different combinations of CPUs, GPUs, DPUs, FPGAs, SmartNICs, and Adaptive SoCs enable the optimization of performance and power for a diverse set of workloads.

comparisons.peer_summary: The company provides advanced technology and IP platforms for customers to design ASICs targeting AI, high-performance computing, and networking applications.
comparisons.comparison: Both companies explicitly target 'AI and high-performance computing' as key application areas for their products, representing complementary infrastructure roles. MU addresses the storage requirement for these workloads, offering SSDs for 'AI data lake applications.' AVGO addresses the custom silicon and processing layer, providing 'Custom Silicon Solutions' for customers to design ASICs 'targeting AI and high-performance computing, networking and storage applications.' Both disclose a strategic focus on enabling this specific computational demand, albeit MU through standard high-performance storage products and AVGO through custom ASIC platforms.

sentences.text: Our 6500 30TB SSDs features high performance, reliability, and endurance for AI data lake applications.
In 2024, we began sampling our 9550 series SSD to meet the growing demands of AI, high-performance computing, and many other workloads.

• Custom Silicon Solutions: We provide advanced technology and intellectual property ("IP") platforms for customers to design and develop application specific integrated circuits ("ASICs") targeting AI and high-performance computing, networking and storage applications. Our custom silicon provides the platform to integrate embedded logic, memory, serializer/deserializer ("SerDes") technology, IP cores and processor cores. ASICs are custom products built to individual customers specifications.

peer_results.rationale: The supplied candidates for INTC (intc_2024_1_D032 and intc_2024_1_D034) focus exclusively on Client CPU and Discrete Client GPU products (e.g., Core Ultra, Arc B-Series) for consumer and thin-and-light markets. They do not contain substantive disclosure regarding Data Center AI, high-performance computing, or storage infrastructure comparable to MU's Item 1 disclosure about Data Center SBU offerings.

comparisons.peer_topic: Data Center Platform Overview and Focus
comparisons.peer_summary: The NVIDIA Data Center platform accelerates compute-intensive workloads like AI and HPC, offering better performance and power efficiency than CPU-only approaches, and is deployed in cloud, on-premises, and edge environments via systems, subsystems, modules, software, and services.
comparisons.comparison: MU and NVDA both highlight the growing demand for AI-driven data center infrastructure, focusing on performance efficiency. MU states that 'growing use of cloud computing and big data analytics is fueling the demand for high performance storage in data centers' and emphasizes 'power efficiency' in its solutions. Similarly, NVDA describes its Data Center platform as focused on accelerating 'compute-intensive workloads, such as AI,' delivering 'significantly better performance and power efficiency relative to conventional CPU-only approaches.' While MU provides the storage layer for these workloads and NVDA provides the compute acceleration, both identify performance and power efficiency as critical differentiators for AI data center deployments.

sentences.text: Data center: The growing use of cloud computing and big data analytics is fueling the demand for high performance storage in data centers.
This fully integrated solution enables improved performance, power efficiency, and security features for data center operators.

The NVIDIA Data Center platform is focused on accelerating the most compute-intensive workloads, such as AI, data analytics, graphics and scientific computing, delivering significantly better performance and power efficiency relative to conventional CPU-only approaches.

peer_results.rationale: The supplied candidates for QCOM (qcom_2024_1_D029 and qcom_2024_1_D020) focus on mobile/edge SoC architecture, on-device AI inference (Hexagon NPU), and automotive autonomous driving features. These topics are distinct from MU's Item 1 disclosure regarding Data Center storage solutions and server-class high-performance storage for AI data lakes.
